prepared_template.title: Respiratory arrest with evolving autonomic and neurological findings
prepared_template.facts:
Presentation and progression
A man in his 40s with longstanding schizophrenia and type 2 diabetes was admitted after an unwitnessed collapse at home. He had reduced alertness and could not follow commands; the initial neurological examination was otherwise unremarkable. Two days after admission he became unstable with fever and respiratory arrest, requiring intubation and ventilation.

By approximately day 10 he remained ventilator-dependent. He could follow simple commands but attention fluctuated. Bradycardia, apnoeas, intermittent fever without an identified infectious correlate, anisocoria and labile BP were documented; isoprenaline and a temporary pacing wire were needed in intensive care. Examination now showed slow horizontal saccades, limited upgaze, spasticity, brisk reflexes, limb clonus, extensor plantar responses and right laterocollis.

Available investigation reports
Routine initial blood results were described as unremarkable except CK 3,120 U/L (reference below 320). CTPA showed a small subsegmental pulmonary embolus. Chest radiography did not show pneumothorax. During ventilation, gas-exchange measures and the A–a gradient were described as within normal limits. Numerical ventilator/gas measurements are not reproduced.

Brain MRI showed bilateral mesial temporal and posterior left thalamic T2-FLAIR high signal. Spinal MRI was normal. CSF contained 30 white cells, 99% lymphocytes, protein 0.55 g/L and glucose 5.1 mmol/L, with IgG index 1.92 (reference below 0.7) and CSF-exclusive oligoclonal bands. The report describes no identified infectious organisms; a complete dated microbiology panel is not reproduced. EEG showed generalised slowing without epileptiform features.

An initial autoimmune encephalitis panel in serum and CSF was reported as negative apart from low-positive GAD65 in serum, undetectable in CSF. The complete panel membership is not supplied here. CT thorax/abdomen/pelvis and whole-body PET-CT were unremarkable, but testicular ultrasound described a heterogeneous left testis with microcalcifications. No tissue diagnosis is provided.

Record limits
The exact ordering of all imaging, CSF and antibody tests is not established. The full medication list, exposure history and timing of any immunotherapy relative to these tests are not supplied. No additional specialist antibody result, definitive tumour histology, treatment response or later outcome is available in this packet.
prepared_template.task:
Audience: a clinician. Use 350–500 words in English, including headings. Assess the supplied records at the stated decision point. Give brief clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.
Use these five sections:
1. Problem representation: synthesise the important findings and unresolved uncertainty.
2. Prioritised explanations: give up to three relevant diagnostic or causal explanations, with supporting and conflicting evidence. Do not force three if fewer are defensible.
3. Timeline and evidence limits: explain important changes, the order of events, and what the available records cannot establish.
4. Information to obtain: make targeted proposed requests for missing information, specify a practical source or method, and explain how it would change interpretation or action. Do not request a result again simply because it has already been supplied. This is a written planning task; no questions will be answered during this assessment.
5. Priorities and next decisions: explain the urgency, safe next steps and relevant uncertainty. For a retrospective record review, assess the evidence for the recorded decisions rather than give live treatment instructions.
Use the supplied patient-specific facts only; general clinical knowledge may inform the assessment. Keep observations, hypotheses and proposals distinct. Unreported information is unknown, not normal. Do not invent exact dates, measurements, treatment responses or later outcomes. Do not provide rubric scores.
prepared_template.reference: Candidate guide: recognise continuing respiratory and autonomic instability requiring intensive monitored care and urgent neurological assessment. Investigate competing reversible/infective and immune causes without declaring the hidden antibody or tumour result known. Specific immunotherapy and tumour-intervention requirements remain awaiting confirmation.
